title.en: Grassroots Democracy – Part 2: Local Government in Rural Areas

text.en: Lakshmanpur has about 200 houses and 700 people, mostly farmers. Some have relatives in the army and some younger villagers have gone to the city for jobs. How will the villagers decide about the school, the well, the road or a land dispute? The answer is the village's own government, the Panchayat.

India has about 600,000 villages, 8,000 towns and over 4,000 cities. M. K. Gandhi said that the real India lives in its villages. A single government cannot manage such a complex society, so local governments handle local issues and give people a direct say in decisions that affect their daily lives.
Every village has a council called the Panchayat, so the system is also called Panchayati Raj, a form of self-government. The Gram Sabha is the group of all adult voters of a village or a few neighbouring villages. It elects the members of the Gram Panchayat, who elect a head called the Sarpanch or Pradhan. Many Gram Panchayats are helped by an officer called the Patwari who keeps land records. Above the Gram Panchayat there are bodies at block and district levels, often called Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad, that coordinate development plans and bring them to the district and State levels. Their duties cover agriculture, housing, roads, water, schools, health, social welfare and culture. Special rules ensure that disadvantaged groups can make their needs heard.
Sarpanchs can transform their villages. Kamble defeated six other candidates, convinced women to attend the Sabha and addressed education and sanitation. Her motto was lok seva, gram seva, service to the village is service to the public. Hiware Bazar in Ahmednagar, Maharashtra, suffered droughts and poor crops. With the cooperation of villagers led by Popatrao Pawar, who got the Padma Shri in 2020, the village became green and prosperous through watershed work.
Panchayats should listen to everyone, including children. Many States have Bal Sabhas and Bal Panchayats. The members persuade parents to send children back to school and not to arrange marriages of girls who should be studying. In Sangkhu Radhu Khandu Gram Panchayat in west Sikkim, the Panchayat built clean school kitchens for mid-day meals. Children aged 8 to 14 took part in parliament-like elections, formed a Cabinet and raised issues such as education and sanitation. The structure of Panchayati Raj varies a little from State to State, but the objective is always the same: to let villagers take an active part in managing their own village.

problem.en: The villagers of Lakshmanpur want a new borewell. Describe how the Panchayat can decide.

text.en: The Gram Sabha meets and every adult voter can speak.
The Gram Panchayat discusses cost and place and decides.
If funds are short, the Panchayat asks the block or district body.

prompt.en: How does the Panchayati Raj system give villagers a say?

requiredIdeas.en: Gram Sabha of all adult voters elects the Gram Panchayat.

points.en: Panchayati Raj is local self-government in villages.
The Gram Sabha elects the Gram Panchayat and its Sarpanch.
Higher bodies coordinate at block and district levels.
Panchayats should listen to children, women and disadvantaged groups.
